title: Refine kernel-routing and prefill/decode scheduling for FlashAttention autotune
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary:
We are observing intermittent latency regressions and throughput drops on high-concurrency workloads after enabling the newer FlashAttention v3 kernels behind the runtime kernel selector. This ticket tracks investigation, targeted tuning of the kernel-routing heuristics, changes to prefill vs decode scheduling, and a conservative rollout plan for the autotuner so we avoid noisy regressions in production.

Background:
- FlashAttention v3 provides better single-op memory usage and faster fused attention for small-to-medium sequence lengths, but in our fleet it occasionally underperforms v2 for long prefill sequences and for workloads with mixed prefill/decode ratios.
- The runtime's kernel selector currently picks kernels based on static heuristics (model size, dtype, and sequence length thresholds) plus an experimental autotuner that samples batches at runtime. After enabling v3 by default for some model families, SLO incidents were observed in customer production traffic (increased p95 latency and lower throughput on p50).

Goals:
- Root cause the regression patterns across sequence-length distributions and concurrency profiles.
- Update kernel-routing heuristics to incorporate prefill/decode tradeoffs (prefill-heavy vs decode-heavy workloads) and KV cache memory pressure signals.
- Harden the autotuner: reduce sampling-induced variance, add safety thresholds, and preferred rollback conditions.
- Validate changes across dedicated and hosted fleets and create an incremental rollout plan with observability hooks.

Acceptance criteria:
- No reproducible p95 latency regression vs baseline for the public test harness across 4 representative workloads (short-chat, long-completion, summarization, streaming Q&A).
- Autotuner sampling disabled by default for production; opt-in rollout with a canary that has automatic rollback on +10% p95 or -5% throughput within 30m.
- New routing policy codified in runtime config with clear tuning knobs: sequence-length breakpoints, memory-pressure thresholds, prefill_ratio cutoff, and per-model preference overrides.
- End-to-end benchmark report (json + plots) and PR that updates our model catalog entries with recommended kernel preferences.

Planned work (high level):
1) Data collection & repro (owners: Liam, Maya)
   - Recreate regression locally with stress harness (mixed prefill/decode with 64/2048 token mixes) and run matrix across batch sizes, seq lengths, and dtype.
   - Capture KV memory footprint, per-kernel op-times, and CUDA occupancy for both v2 and v3.
2) Heuristic improvements (owners: Liam, Jorge)
   - Introduce a prefill_ratio signal: fraction of tokens from prefill vs decode over sliding window.
   - Adjust kernel thresholds: e.g., force v2 for prefill sequences > 1024 when prefill_ratio > 0.6 and observed KV pressure > 75%.
3) Autotuner changes (owners: Jorge, Sima)
   - Reduce sampling frequency and increase sample-size to lower variance (sample 10 requests every 30s per model variant in canary).
   - Add asymmetric cost function that prefers lower p95 over micro p50 wins.
   - Safety: require 3 consecutive sample windows showing improvement before committing route change.
4) Scheduling changes (owners: Maya, Infrastructure)
   - Prioritize prefill batches to consolidating GPU kernel launch patterns (coalesced prefill passes) to reduce kernel-launch overhead.
   - Separate prefill and decode queues in the scheduler to avoid interleaving that degrades kernel fusion opportunities.
5) Testing and rollout (owners: SRE, Growth)
   - Canary: 2% traffic, 4 hours observation, automated rollback on thresholds.
   - Staged ramp to 25% -> 100% with monitoring for model-specific anomalies.

Technical notes & tradeoffs:
- Forcing v2 on long prefill sequences increases memory headroom and can allow larger batch coalescing but may reduce token/sec for decode-only streaming workloads where v3 excels. We mitigate by making the rule context-aware (only when prefill_ratio high and memory_pressure above threshold).
- Separating queues increases scheduler complexity and could increase tail latency if not tuned; we'll run integration tests in the staging cluster with production-like load.
- Autotuner conservative mode reduces opportunistic wins but significantly lowers risk of noisy regressions; acceptable for initial rollout.

Benchmarks to produce:
- Per-model 95th/50th latency and throughput matrix across seq lengths [32,128,512,1024,2048] and batch sizes [1,4,8,16].
- KV cache memory usage and CUDA memory fragmentation before/after routing change.
- Autotuner decision traces (time-series of chosen kernel per model, sample windows, decision confidence).

- Stress harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime-stress
- Initial regression incident runbook: https://drive.company.com/regressions/RA-2025-02-flashattn-v3
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6012 (WIP - kernel-routing POC)
- Benchmark dashboard (staging): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/runtime-kernel-tuning

Follow-ups / future work:
- Explore mixed-precision micro-kernel variants and quantization-aware kernel selection.
- Add ML-driven selector that learns per-model kernel preferences from historical telemetry.
